assertions.description: WebTransportError is exposed in this secure context and its prototype chain inherits from DOMException.
new WebTransportError(message, {source, streamErrorCode}) sets name "WebTransportError", the message, source and streamErrorCode, with legacy code 0.
assertions.test: (() => { const e = new WebTransportError('m', { source: 'session', streamErrorCode: 70000 }); return e.name === 'WebTransportError' && e.message === 'm' && e.source === 'session' && e.streamErrorCode === 70000 && e.code === 0; })()

assertions.description: With only a message, the WebTransportErrorOptions defaults apply: source is "stream" and streamErrorCode is null.
assertions.test: (() => { const e = new WebTransportError('only a message'); return e.message === 'only a message' && e.source === 'stream' && e.streamErrorCode === null; })()

assertions.description: streamErrorCode is a [Clamp] unsigned long: 4294967295 and 65536 are kept, 2**32 saturates to 4294967295 and -1 to 0, without throwing.
assertions.test: (() => { const c = (v) => new WebTransportError('m', { streamErrorCode: v }).streamErrorCode; return c(4294967295) === 4294967295 && c(65536) === 65536 && c(2 ** 32) === 4294967295 && c(-1) === 0; })()

assertions.description: The standard constructor accepts a string message but rejects a source outside the WebTransportErrorSource enum with TypeError.
assertions.test: (() => { try { if (new WebTransportError('m').message !== 'm') return false; } catch (e) { return false; } try { new WebTransportError('m', { source: 'nope' }); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: Chromium compatibility overload: new WebTransportError({message, streamErrorCode}) still works, with source "stream" and the octet code clamped (300 -> 255). Chromium-specific; a spec-only engine stringifies the object.
assertions.test: (() => { const a = new WebTransportError({ message: 'x', streamErrorCode: 3 }); const b = new WebTransportError({ message: 'y', streamErrorCode: 300 }); return a.message === 'x' && a.streamErrorCode === 3 && a.source === 'stream' && b.streamErrorCode === 255; })()

assertions.description: structuredClone(new WebTransportError('m', {source: 'stream', streamErrorCode: 4294967295})) returns a WebTransportError with the same message, source and 32-bit code (no DataCloneError).
assertions.test: (() => { const c = structuredClone(new WebTransportError('m', { source: 'stream', streamErrorCode: 4294967295 })); return c instanceof WebTransportError && c.name === 'WebTransportError' && c.message === 'm' && c.source === 'stream' && c.streamErrorCode === 4294967295; })()

assertions.description: A session error's null streamErrorCode survives structured cloning as null (not 0), along with source "session".
assertions.test: (() => { const c = structuredClone(new WebTransportError('closed', { source: 'session' })); return c instanceof WebTransportError && c.source === 'session' && c.streamErrorCode === null; })()

assertions.description: A WebTransportError written to IndexedDB while serialization is enabled is still read back as a WebTransportError after relaunching with the writer kill switch off.
assertions.test: Needs two launches of a build with the change: write via /v159/webtransporterror-api-alignment-and-serialization/reconnect-diagnostics/, then relaunch with --disable-blink-features=WebTransportErrorSerialization and reload — the stored record must read back natively while new writes fall back.

assertions.description: writer.abort(new WebTransportError('', {streamErrorCode: 70000})) on a WebTransport stream reaches the peer as application code 70000 (no 8-bit narrowing).
assertions.test: Requires a live HTTP/3 WebTransport server that can log received RESET_STREAM / STOP_SENDING codes; this site cannot host one.
